title: M2: ticktimer sys_clock driver
description: Zephyr machine-timer driver is unusable (no CLINT). sys_clock = MMIO driver on 64-bit ticktimer @0xE001B000: free-run + one-shot compare alarm, IRQ 20 — same model as the Xous kernel clock (xous-ticktimer service). Alternative: timer0 @0xE001C000 (32-bit down-counter w/ auto-reload) as fallback/periodic mode. Register names in utralib bao1x.rs:2047-2080. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §3.
acceptance_criteria: CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC behaves; k_uptime/k_sleep accurate; tickless idle works or is documented why not.

title: M2: DUART poll-mode console driver
description: Poll-only DUART @0x40042000 (separate from the 4 UDMA UARTs). Boot1 leaves it configured @1Mbaud 8N1 on PB14/PB13 — inherit, don't re-init initially. Register names from utralib DUART block; behavioral reference: xous baremetal/bao1x-boot console. Add baochip,duart DT binding + console driver in zephyr-baochip drivers/serial.
acceptance_criteria: printk/k_msg output visible on the PB14 serial line (or sim's debug UART) from a running Zephyr image.

title: M2: irqarray interrupt controller driver
description: Custom ExternalInterruptArray: no CLINT/PLIC. 20 LiteX irqarray banks + ticktimer(20)/susres(21)/mailbox(22,23)/timer0(30); flat event index n → bank n/16, bit n%16. Custom CSRs: MIM 0xBC0/MIP 0xFC0 (inverse-logic mask), SIM 0x9C0/SIP 0xDC0. Mirror soc/litex/litex_vexriscv intc driver shape (overrides arch_irq_*). RISK R3: edge-vs-level ack semantics undocumented — mirror Xous kernel ack sequence exactly, test each bank in verilator sim. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §4.
acceptance_criteria: IRQs from at least two banks + ticktimer dispatch and ack correctly under load; nested/priority behavior sane.

title: M2: console + clock — DUART console, irqarray intc, ticktimer sys_clock
description: Make it a real OS. (1) DUART poll console driver @0x40042000 (boot1 leaves it live @1Mbaud on PB14/PB13) — fastest path to printf. (2) intc driver: 20 LiteX irqarray event banks, flat index n → bank n/16 bit n%16, custom CSRs MIM 0xBC0/MIP 0xFC0 (inverse-logic mask), SIM 0x9C0/SIP 0xDC0; validate edge-vs-level ack semantics against Xous kernel usage (risk R3). (3) ticktimer sys_clock @0xE001B000 (64-bit free-run + one-shot compare alarm, IRQ 20) per xous-ticktimer implementation. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §3-4.
acceptance_criteria: Preemptive scheduling demonstrable: console prints, threads time-slice on ticktimer interrupts, IRQs from multiple banks dispatch correctly.

title: M1: soc/baochip/bao1x skeleton + 0x60060400 linker layout
description: SoC port skeleton in zephyr-baochip modeled on soc/litex/litex_vexriscv (4 files + soc.yml; no CLINT/PLIC needed — bao intc is MMIO + custom CSRs MIM/MIP 0xBC0/0xFC0). Files: soc.yml, Kconfig(.soc/.defconfig w/ CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_UF2_FAMILY_ID=0xa7d76373), CMakeLists.txt, soc.h, custom linker fragment (ROM ORIGIN 0x60060400 LENGTH ~0x3F800, RAM ACRAM 0x61000000/2MiB, reset code FIRST linked byte for the JAL chain: sigblock jal +768, presign[0]=0x1000006f). Entry must reset mtvec/sp (boot1 leftovers), assumes M-mode/MMU-off/IRQs-masked/a0=KERNEL_START/a1=0. Details: .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §1, §7; .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §3.
acceptance_criteria: Zephyr links for bao1x with _start exactly at 0x60060400 (verified via readelf/nm), image fits baremetal slot budget, CSR accessor shims compile against hal_bao/include/bao1x_peri.h.

title: M1: .data-capable image packer + devkey signer in hal_bao/tools
description: Plan-changing tooling item (risk R1). Stock xous-copy-object strips .data (poke table ≤40 words) — Zephyr needs a packer that embeds .data LMA in ROM and lets the kernel self-copy on start. Wrap/sign with xous-sign-image --bao1x --with-jump --sig-length 768 --function-code baremetal --loader-key devkey/dev.key (run inside xous-core for git-describe, or pass --git-describe). UF2: family 0xa7d76373, 256B payload/512B block, base 0x60060000. Spec: .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §4-6.
acceptance_criteria: Packer consumes a Zephyr ELF, emits signed UF2 that boot1 accepts on the BAOCHIP volume; verified in verilator sim and on hardware.

title: M0: scaffolding — vendor prefix, toolchain smoke test, regen path
description: Tree hygiene and toolchain validation before any SoC code. (1) Add 'baochip' to dts/bindings/vendor-prefixes.txt in zephyr-baochip + REUSE/spdx headers on new files. (2) Vendored bao1x_peri.h/.svd already in hal_bao/include (PROVENANCE.md records regen: rtl_to_svd.py --path ../../). (3) Toolchain smoke test: Zephyr SDK riscv64-zephyr-elf builds rv32imac_zicsr (gd32vf103 precedent, .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §5).
acceptance_criteria: A trivial riscv32 Zephyr build passes with the SDK toolchain; vendor prefix registered; every new file carries an SPDX tag.

title: M1: boot to main — SoC skeleton, linker, .data-capable packer, signed UF2
description: The JAL-chain hump. (1) soc/baochip/bao1x in zephyr-baochip: soc.yml, Kconfig(.soc/.defconfig incl UF2 family id 0xa7d76373), CMakeLists, soc.h, custom linker — ROM ORIGIN 0x60060400 LENGTH ~0x3F800, RAM 0x61000000/2MiB; reset code must be the FIRST linked byte (sigblock jal +768, presign[0]=0x1000006f). (2) tools/ in hal_bao: custom image packer embedding .data LMA in ROM (stock xous-copy-object strips .data — ≤40-word poke table) + devkey signer (xous-sign-image --bao1x --with-jump --sig-length 768 --function-code baremetal --loader-key devkey/dev.key). (3) Handoff assumptions: M-mode, MMU off, IRQs masked, a0=KERNEL_START/a1=0, ~350MHz, DUART live, mtvec/sp must be reset (boot1 leftovers). Details: .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md.
acceptance_criteria: Signed UF2 image boots on Dabao (or verilator sim linked at RRAM base with --boot-offset 0) and reaches early shell/zephyr-entry; readelf confirms _start at 0x60060400 and .data present in ROM.

title: [epic] Zephyr RTOS port for Baochip 1x SoC and Dabao board
description: Port Zephyr RTOS to the Baochip 1x SoC (BAO1X2S4F-WA, VexRiscv RV32IMAC+Zkn, Sv32, no CLINT/PLIC) and the Dabao development board. Whole-SoC port, not a board port: the chip's only existing OS is Xous (Rust); there is no vendor C SDK. Zephyr code lands as new files in the zephyr-baochip fork; hal_bao holds vendored headers, image tooling, tickets, design docs. Reference implementation for all hardware behavior is xous-core. Full story: .design/init/init.md. Decisions/risks: .design/research/04-synthesis.md.
acceptance_criteria: hello_world boots on Dabao hardware via devkey-signed UF2 copied to the BAOCHIP MSC volume, with console on DUART (PB14/PB13 @1Mbaud), preemptive scheduling on ticktimer sys_clock, GPIO buttons readable, and the image toolchain (packer + signer + UF2) reproducible from hal_bao.

title: Investigate: irqarray edge-vs-level ack semantics from Xous kernel
description: Risk R3 from 04-synthesis.md: irqarray ack semantics undocumented; wrong assumptions = lost or re-entrant IRQs. Trace the Xous kernel IRQ path (kernel/src) + per-peripheral drivers (uart, gpio, ticktimer) for the exact ack order (status-clear before/after handler, level vs pulse). Deliver an ack-contract note for the intc driver author.
acceptance_criteria: Ack-order contract documented with citations into xous-core; encoded as comments/assertions in the intc driver

title: Investigate: baremetal slot budget / RRAM layout growth path
description: Risk R2 + open question 1 from 04-synthesis.md: baremetal slot caps at ~254KiB before Xous kernel @0x6009FD00. Determine (a) whether boot1 slot config allows a larger baremetal region or relocation, (b) what a Zephyr image with console+intc+timer+gpio realistically sizes at, (c) whether XIP-only (.text in RRAM, .data in ACRAM) keeps us under budget. Sources: bao1x-boot slot config, baremetal/src/platform/bao1x/link.x.
acceptance_criteria: Written answer in .design/research/ with measured image sizes; go/no-go on slot renegotiation

title: M4: UDMA subsystem + interrupt-driven UART console
description: Descriptor-DMA subsystem shared by 4 UARTs + SPI/I2C/I2S: descriptor ring handling, channel arbitration, then UART2 interrupt console (the real console on PB14/PB13 — replaces DUART poll mode). Custom IP, reference = xous bao1x-hal UDMA drivers. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §5.
acceptance_criteria: UART console in interrupt mode; SPI or I2C channel demonstrably talks to external hardware

title: M4: comms — UDMA subsystem, interrupt UART console, serial uploader
description: UDMA descriptor-DMA subsystem driver (custom IP; 4 UARTs + SPI/I2C/I2S channels behind it): shared descriptor handling first, then interrupt-driven UART2 console (the real console, PB14/PB13), then SPI/I2C as board needs demand. Optional: boot1 REPL 'uf2 <base64>' serial uploader (bio-loader pattern) for CI-less flashing. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §5; .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §7.
acceptance_criteria: UART console works in interrupt mode; at least one SPI or I2C peripheral talks to an external device; serial flasher documented.

title: M3: boards/baochip/dabao HWMv2 board definition
description: board.yml, devicetree (IOX gpio, duart console, ticktimer, wdt, rtc, buttons), Kconfig*, board.cmake referencing uf2 runner, image defs. Dissect one modern minimal riscv board under boards/ as template (.design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §2, §7 skeleton).
acceptance_criteria: west build -b baochip/dabao/some-variant samples/hello_world succeeds end-to-end

title: M3: IOX GPIO driver
description: IOX @0x5012F000: 6 ports PA-PF × 16 pins, 2-bit AFSEL, pull-up only, IRQs via INTCR/INTFR → PIOIRQ0-3. DT binding baochip,iox-gpio + Zephyr GPIO driver API. Reserved boot pins PC13 (PROG/USB-SE0), PB13/PB14 (console) must be documented/protected. Reference: utralib IOX block + xous gpio service.
acceptance_criteria: gpio_api/test suite passes (subset valid on-board); button input + header pad toggle verified

title: M3: board completeness — Dabao HWMv2 tree, GPIO, WDT, RTC
description: boards/baochip/dabao in zephyr-baochip: board.yml, DTS (IOX gpio@0x5012F000, duart, ticktimer, wdt, rtc, buttons RST_N/PC13), Kconfig, board.cmake w/ uf2 runner. Plus drivers: IOX GPIO (6 banks PA-PF × 16 pins, 2-bit AFSEL, pull-up only, INTCR/INTFR → PIOIRQ0-3), CMSDK WDT @0x40041000 (unlock 0x1ACCE551, feed 0x5A — standard IP, cheap win), PL031 RTC @0x40061000. NO LEDs on Dabao — blinky = UART print + button. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §6-7; .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §2.
acceptance_criteria: west build -b baochip/dabao samples/hello_world produces flashable image; button sample reads PC13/RST; GPIO toggle observable on header pads; WDT feed keeps system alive.

title: M5: long tail — USB, BIO/SCE, Rust sample, Renode, upstreaming
description: Deferred work after the port is alive: USB CDC-ACM device driver (Corigine xHCI-style controller w/ USB3 caps — hard; bootloader stack not app-reusable), BIO coprocessor (4× PicoRV32 w/ FIFOs/IMEM/quantum) and SCE crypto (AES/SHA/PKE/TRNG/keyslots) as custom Zephyr subsystems, Rust app sample via zephyr-lang-rust module, Renode platform model (none exists today; verilator sim is the interim), Zkn exposure via riscv,isa-extensions, hal_bao split-out decision, and upstreaming to zephyrproject-rtos. Details: .design/research/03-rust-survey.md; .design/research/04-synthesis.md M5 + open questions.
acceptance_criteria: Picked off opportunistically; each gets its own ticket when activated

title: M4: boot1 REPL serial uploader (optional)
description: boot1 serial console accepts 'uf2 <base64 block-per-line>' writes to RRAM with same range/family checks as MSC — a bio-loader-style Python uploader enables headless/CI flashing without mount/unmount dance. Details: .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §7.
acceptance_criteria: Python script flashes a signed image to a Dabao over /dev/ttyACM* without manual volume mounting

title: M3: CMSDK watchdog + PL031 RTC drivers
description: Two standard-IP cheap wins: WDT = ARM CMSDK @0x40041000 (unlock 0x1ACCE551, feed 0x5A; Xous runs ~30s period fed from ticktimer — wdt.rs:22-60,116); RTC = PL031 @0x4006100. Both have in-tree Zephyr analogues/bindings to adapt (CMSDK WDT driver exists for ARM boards; PL031 too). Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §3.
acceptance_criteria: wdt feed via sys_clock works; rtc readable, settable, alarm IRQ optional
